40889-tyrol-and-its-people.title: And Its People
40889-tyrol-and-its-people.creator: Clive Holland
40889-tyrol-and-its-people.description: A book by Clive Holland. 's thanks are given for permission to reproduce some beautiful photographs of Tyrol scenery and Tyrolese subjects in place of less pictorial work by the author himself. To many others, who gave information to the author during his travels in Tyrol, relating to many interesting matters, acknowledgment is also here gratefully made.

arxiv-2108-12232.title: A thirteen-year-long broadband view of BL Lac 2015 A thirteen-year-long broadband view of BL Lac – References
arxiv-2108-12232.creator: N. Sahakyan, P. Giommi
arxiv-2108-12232.description: Abstract We present the results of an extensive analysis of the optical, ultraviolet, X-ray and γ \gamma -ray data collected from the observations of the BL Lac objects prototype BL Lacertae carried out over a period of nearly 13 years, between August 2008 and March 2021.

arxiv-2111-08916.title: Alternative Paradigms of Computation
arxiv-2111-08916.creator: William Gasarch, Nathan Hayes, Emily Kaplitz, William Regli
arxiv-2111-08916.description: Abstract With Moore’s law coming to a close it is useful to look at other forms of computer hardware. In this paper we survey what is known about several modes of computation: Neuromorphic, Custom Logic, Quantum, Optical, Spintronics, Reversible, Many-Valued Logic, Chemical, DNA, Neurological, Fluidic, Amorphous, Thermodynamic, Peptide, and Membrane.

arxiv-2206-03002.title: Stationary states in two lane traffic: insights from kinetic theory
arxiv-2206-03002.creator: A. Sai Venkata Ramana, Saif Eddin Jabari
arxiv-2206-03002.description: Abstract Kinetics of dilute heterogeneous traffic on a two lane road is formulated in the framework of Ben-Naim Krapivsky model and stationary state properties are analytically derived in the asymptotic limit. The heterogeneity is introduced into the model as a quenched disorder in desired speeds of vehicles.

arxiv-2207-01579.title: Spatiotemporal Feature Learning Based on Two-Step LSTM and Transformer for CT Scans
arxiv-2207-01579.creator: Chih-Chung Hsu, Chi-Han Tsai, Guan-Lin Chen, Sin-Di Ma, Shen-Chieh Tai
arxiv-2207-01579.description: Abstract Computed tomography (CT) imaging could be very practical for diagnosing various diseases. However, the nature of the CT images is even more diverse since the resolution and number of the slices of a CT scan are determined by the machine and its settings.

arxiv-2208-12688.title: Generalised Baumslag-Solitar groups and Hierarchically Hyperbolic Groups
arxiv-2208-12688.creator: J. O. Button
arxiv-2208-12688.description: Abstract We look at isometric actions on arbitrary hyperbolic spaces of generalised Baumslag - Solitar groups of arbitrary dimension (the rank of the free abelian vertex and edge subgroups). It is known that being a hierarchically hyperbolic group is not a quasi-isometric invariant.

arxiv-2301-11322.title: Semi-Automated Construction of Food Composition Knowledge Base
arxiv-2301-11322.creator: Jason Youn, Fangzhou Li, Ilias Tagkopoulos
arxiv-2301-11322.description: Abstract A food composition knowledge base, which stores the essential phyto-, micro-, and macro-nutrients of foods is useful for both research and industrial applications. Although many existing knowledge bases attempt to curate such information, they are often limited by time-consuming manual curation processes.

arxiv-2407-12375.title: FETCH: A Memory-Efficient Replay Approach for Continual Learning in Image Classification
arxiv-2407-12375.creator: Markus Weißflog, Peter Protzel, Peer Neubert
arxiv-2407-12375.description: Abstract Class-incremental continual learning is an important area of research, as static deep learning methods fail to adapt to changing tasks and data distributions. In previous works, promising results were achieved using replay and compressed replay techniques. In the field of regular replay, GDumb [ 23 ] achieved outstanding results but requires a large amount of memory.

arxiv-2407-15727.title: Inferring turbulent velocity and temperature fields and their statistics from Lagrangian velocity measurements using physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
arxiv-2407-15727.creator: Juan Diego Toscano, Theo Käufer, Zhibo Wang, Martin Maxey, Christian Cierpka, George Em Karniadakis
arxiv-2407-15727.description: Abstract We propose the Artificial Intelligence Velocimetry-Thermometry (AIVT) method to infer hidden temperature fields from experimental turbulent velocity data. This physics-informed machine learning method enables us to infer continuous temperature fields using only sparse velocity data, hence eliminating the need for direct temperature measurements.

arxiv-2503-01374.title: Verifying QUIC implementations using Ivy Conference: Virtual Conference; 2021
arxiv-2503-01374.creator: Christophe Crochet, Tom Rousseaux, J-F Sambon, Maxime Piraux, Axel Legay
arxiv-2503-01374.description: Abstract . QUIC is a new transport protocol combining the reliability and congestion control features of TCP with the security features of TLS . One of the main challenges with QUIC is to guarantee that any of its implementation follows the IETF specification.

arxiv-2506-00703.title: Adaptive Traffic-Following Scheme for Orderly Distributed Control of Multi-Vehicle Systems Thanks: This work was funded by NASA’s Convergent Aeronautics Solutions and Transformative Tools and Technologies projects.
arxiv-2506-00703.creator: Anahita Jain, Husni Idris, John-Paul Clarke, Daniel Delahaye
arxiv-2506-00703.description: Abstract We present an adaptive control scheme to enable the emergence of order within distributed, autonomous multi-agent systems. Past studies showed that under high-density conditions, order generated from traffic-following behavior reduces travel times, while under low densities, choosing direct paths is more beneficial.

arxiv-2508-11754.title: Theory of Exozodi Sources and Dust Evolution
arxiv-2508-11754.creator: Mark C. Wyatt, Tim D. Pearce, Nicole Pawellek, Sarah Dodson-Robinson, Virginie C. Faramaz-Gorka, Isabel Rebollido, Jessica K. Rigley, Christopher C. Stark
arxiv-2508-11754.description: Abstract Exozodiacal dust disks (exozodis) are populations of warm ( ∼ 300 ​ K \sim 300\;{\rm K} ) or hot ( ∼ 1000 ​ K \sim 1000\;{\rm K} ) dust, located in or interior to a star’s habitable zone, detected around ∼ 25 \sim 25 % of main-sequence stars as excess emission over the stellar photosphere at mid- or near-infrared

arxiv-2510-01954.title: Patch-as-Decodable-Token: Towards Unified Multi-Modal Vision Tasks in MLLMs
arxiv-2510-01954.creator: Yongyi Su, Haojie Zhang, Shijie Li, Nanqing Liu, Jingyi Liao, Junyi Pan, Yuan Liu, Xiaofen Xing, Chong Sun, Chen Li, Nancy F. Chen, Shuicheng Yan, Xulei Yang, Xun Xu
arxiv-2510-01954.description: Abstract Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced rapidly in recent years. However, existing approaches for vision tasks often rely on indirect representations, such as generating coordinates as text for detection, which limits performance and prevents dense prediction tasks like segmentation.

arxiv-2510-09352.title: LR-WaveHoltz: A Low-Rank Helmholtz Solver
arxiv-2510-09352.creator: Andreas Granath, Daniel Appelö, Siyang Wang
arxiv-2510-09352.description: Abstract We propose a low-rank method for solving the Helmholtz equation. Our approach is based on the WaveHoltz method, which computes Helmholtz solutions by applying a time-domain filter to the solution of a related wave equation. The wave equation is discretized by high-order multiblock summation-by-parts finite differences.

arxiv-2510-18105.title: Virus Spreading in Quantum Networks
arxiv-2510-18105.creator: Junpeng Hou, Mark Maximilian Seidel, Chuanwei Zhang
arxiv-2510-18105.description: Abstract Recent advances in quantum communication have enabled long-distance secure information transfer through quantum channels, giving rise to quantum networks with unique physical and statistical properties. However, as in classical networks, the propagation of viruses in these systems could have severe consequences. Here, we investigate the critical problem of virus spreading in quantum networks.

arxiv-2512-24755.title: Trustworthy Equipment Monitoring via Cascaded Anomaly Detection and Thermal Localization
arxiv-2512-24755.creator: Sungwoo Kang
arxiv-2512-24755.description: Abstract Predictive maintenance in industrial settings demands not only accurate anomaly detection but also interpretable explanations that maintenance engineers can trust and act upon. While multimodal fusion approaches combining sensor time-series with thermal imagery have shown promise, we demonstrate through extensive ablation studies that naive fusion strategies can actually degrade detection performance.

arxiv-2601-22325.title: Chirality and Clock transitions in Twisted Dipolar Clusters
arxiv-2601-22325.creator: Paula Mellado, Xavier Cazor, Andres Concha
arxiv-2601-22325.description: Abstract We study samples and a dipolar model of magnetic rods arranged on twisted polygonal clusters in terms of the twist angle. We find that the relative twist between polygons induces noncollinear chiral phases, ranging from flux vortex closure to hedgehog like radial configurations.

openalex-w7215034230.description: This article aimed to analyze, based on the narratives of older adults who experienced schooling in rural contexts, the relationships between schooling conditions, experiences with reading and writing, and knowledge constructed throughout life. This qualitative study derives...

pmc-10505335.title: Constructing phylogenetic networks via cherry picking and machine learning
pmc-10505335.creator: Giulia Bernardini, Leo van Iersel, Esther Julien, Leen Stougie
pmc-10505335.description: BackgroundCombining a set of phylogenetic trees into a single phylogenetic network that explains all of them is a fundamental challenge in evolutionary studies. Existing methods are computationally expensive and can either handle only small numbers of phylogenetic trees or are limited to severely restricted classes of networks.

pmc-10601374.title: Presynaptic Kainate Receptors onto Somatostatin Interneurons Are Recruited by Activity throughout Development and Contribute to Cortical Sensory Adaptation
pmc-10601374.creator: Tevye J. Stachniak, Ali Ö. Argunsah, Jenq-Wei Yang, Linbi Cai, Theofanis Karayannis
pmc-10601374.description: Somatostatin (SST) interneurons produce delayed inhibition because of the short-term facilitation of their excitatory inputs created by the expression of metabotropic glutamate receptor 7 (mGluR7) and presynaptic GluK2-containing kainate receptors (GluK2-KARs). Using mice of both sexes, we find that as synaptic facilitation at layer (L)2/3 SST cell inputs increases during the first few postnatal weeks, so does GluK2-KAR expression.

pmc-11365510.title: Changes in Ocular Blood Flow After Intravitreal Injection for Diabetic Macular Edema Between Aflibercept and Faricimab
pmc-11365510.creator: Takahiro Mizukami, Saya Mizumoto, Takuya Ishibashi, Satoru Ueno, Takayo Toyonishi, Kuniko Tachibana, Soichiro Mishima, Yoshikazu Shimomura
pmc-11365510.description: PurposeIn this study, we aimed to evaluate and compare the effects of intravitreal aflibercept (IVA) and intravitreal faricimab (IVF) injections on the blood flow of retinal vessels in the peripapillary region and optic nerve head (ONH) in eyes with diabetic macular edema (DME) using laser speckle flowgraphy (LSFG).

pmc-11454025.title: 7948 Integration of Epigenomics and Metabolomics Reveals New Signaling in Aggressive Thyroid Cancer
pmc-11454025.creator: A Sanghi, S Wu, T Chou, L A Orloff, M Kasowski, M Snyder
pmc-11454025.description: Disclosure: A. Sanghi: None. S. Wu: None. T. Chou: None. L.A. Orloff: None. M. Kasowski: None. M. Snyder: None.Although genetic mutations are causal in human cancers, the contribution of chromatin changes to cancer onset and progression remains less well understood.

pmc-12583357.title: Hyperspectral imaging of grains uncovers the genetic architecture of nitrogen response of development in bread wheat
pmc-12583357.creator: Qiang Liu, Yinyin Zhang, Jiawei Shi, Wanneng Yang, Hui Feng, Weijuan Hu
pmc-12583357.description: Unraveling the genetic architecture of nitrogen response of development is critical for improving wheat productivity while reducing nitrogen inputs. In this study, hyperspectral imaging (HSI) was applied to wheat grains obtained from nitrogen-deficient and normal conditions, combined with genome-wide association studies (GWAS), to investigate the nitrogen response of development in a diverse wheat panel.

pmc-12606162.title: Analysis and reinforcement design of power concentrated joints in steel arch splicing mechanisms for tunnel boring machines
pmc-12606162.creator: Xinyi Yu, Yuanfu He, Zhen Xu, Xiangpan Zheng
pmc-12606162.description: To address the challenges of low efficiency and high safety risks in manual steel arch installation during Tunnel Boring Machine (TBM) construction, this study proposes an innovative steel arch splicing mechanism. By employing power-concentrated joint analysis and closed-loop reinforcement design, the mechanism demonstrates significantly enhanced dynamic performance and load-bearing capacity.

pmc-13055033.title: Assessment of visual contrast sensitivity in biotoxin-exposed individuals using four testing methods
pmc-13055033.creator: Ingrid Astrid Jimenez-Barbosa, Sean Di Lizio, Seong Beom Ahn, Benjamin Heng, Janet Kim, Amanda J Watson, Sieu K Khuu
pmc-13055033.description: BackgroundEnvironmental biotoxins, such as mould, are linked to neurological and visual dysfunction, including impaired visual contrast sensitivity (VCS). Testing VCS alterations is recommended as a biomarker for biotoxicity. This study compared four VCS tests in detecting VCS deficits in individuals with clinical signs of biotoxicity.

pmc-13069683.title: MYC and AP-1 oncogenes cooperatively bind enhancers to rewire transcription
pmc-13069683.creator: Reshma Kalyan Sundaram, Kshitiz Parihar, Stephanie Monson, Ravi Radhakrishnan, Bomyi Lim
pmc-13069683.description: The transcription factor c-MYC (MYC) is deregulated in ~70% of human cancers. Through de novo motif discovery analysis on published MYC ChIP-seq datasets from cancer cell lines, we found cell-type-specific co-enrichment of the TRE motifs (AP-1 binding sites) alongside MYC’s canonical EBOX motif.
